description: Juicy, tender poached chicken breasts for shredding, slicing, salads and meal prep.

ingredients.name: cold water or low-sodium chicken broth (just enough to cover by 1 inch)

notes:
Go by temperature, not the clock: pull at 160°F. Overcooking is what makes it rubbery.
Never let it boil hard once the chicken is cooking. If your burner keeps the pot too hot after turning off (common on electric stoves), slide it to a cool burner.
If it hasn't reached 160°F after 20 minutes, put it back on low heat at a bare simmer, lid cracked, and check every 2–3 minutes.
Frozen breasts: skip the off-heat method and hold at a bare simmer instead, checking temperature from about 18 minutes.
Strain and save the cooking liquid as a light stock for soups or rice.
Keeps 3–4 days in the fridge; store shredded chicken with a splash of the broth to stay moist.
To shred: let the chicken rest 5 minutes, then shred it while still warm, since it pulls apart much more easily than cold chicken. Two forks work well: hold the breast steady with one and drag the other along the grain. For a big batch, put the warm breasts in a container with a tight lid and shake hard for 20–30 seconds, and they'll mostly shred themselves.

source.label: Cooking question in the Recipes chat

steps.title: Even out the chicken
steps.text: If {0} are much thicker at one end, pound the thick end to an even thickness (about ¾ inch) so they cook evenly.

steps.title: Set up the pot
steps.text: Lay the chicken in a single layer in a medium pot. Add {1}, using just enough to cover by about an inch, then add {2}, {3}, {4}, {5} and {6}.

steps.title: Bring to a boil
steps.text: Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, uncovered, skimming off any foam. This can take 10–15 minutes; the chicken is already cooking during this time.

steps.title: Turn off the heat and cover
steps.text: As soon as it reaches a boil, turn off the heat, cover the pot and leave it on the burner. Start checking at 12 minutes and pull each breast when the thickest part reads 160°F on an instant-read thermometer (usually 12–18 minutes).

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Rest the chicken 5 minutes; it will coast up to 165°F. For shredding or meal prep, let it rest in the warm liquid for 10 minutes instead so it stays juicier. Then slice or shred.

title: Rosemary Sourdough Focaccia
description: Overnight sourdough focaccia in a 9×13 pan — fluffy inside, crisp outside, topped with rosemary and finishing salt and brushed with garlic butter.

source.label: Sam @ saltnsprinkles on TikTok (shared by samanthagee23); full recipe verified on saltnsprinkles.com

time: About 21 hours (mostly hands-off; start the day before)

steps.text: Lift a corner of the dough, stretch it up and fold it over the center. Turn the bowl a quarter turn and repeat 15–20 times. This is the only stretch-and-fold session.

steps.text: Cover loosely with a towel and leave at room temperature until just about doubled (up to about 8 hours, depending on your starter and kitchen).

notes:
Use active starter, not discard.
Bread flour gives a chewier crumb; all-purpose works too.
The original doesn't measure the olive oil — 3 tbsp is a starting point; be generous with the pan.
Store at room temperature in an airtight container 2–3 days (not the fridge). Reheat slices in a toaster or at 375°F for 5–10 minutes.
